novelty.justification: The claim reframes factual storage as a per-fact quantity—"the number of independent components that each suffice to support recall"—and predicts that this redundancy governs edit "snap back," noise tolerance, and frequency, so its novelty route is primarily a new measurement and mechanistic relationship rather than a new setting. Searches using "LLM factual knowledge redundancy minimal ablation set," "knowledge neurons distributed facts edit resistance," and "causal tracing localization editing" found closest overlap in Hase et al., "Does Localization Inform Editing?" and the ICLR 2024 paper "What does the Knowledge Neuron Thesis Have to do with Knowledge?," which question localization and connect causal loci to editing but do not define a minimal independent-locus count or make it the shared predictor of editing and noise robustness. Moving from those works to a per-fact ablation redundancy measure is a substantive natural extension and multi-step operationalization of existing distributed-representation and fault-tolerance ideas, rather than a wholly new core interpretability paradigm. The combined prediction is not merely a renamed standard method, but its central direction is sufficiently suggested by prior findings that distributed representations survive localized interventions, placing it in the upper standard-novelty band rather than 7–8.
